name: Blur
hook: Took Ray Davies' observational English songwriting and rebuilt it for a country arguing about Britpop and class in the 1990s.
blurb: Blur formed in London in 1988. Damon Albarn has repeatedly named the Kinks, and especially Ray Davies' wry, observational songwriting, as a direct influence on how he wrote about English life, and he has said in interviews that 'Waterloo Sunset' is the song he wishes he had written. He has even performed it on stage with Davies himself. That makes Blur the clearest heir on this map to the close, specific way of writing about English class and place that Davies started, and their mid-1990s albums, 'Parklife' (1994) especially, are where it shows most.

signatureTracks.title: Parklife
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The title track most directly working the Kinks' observational, character-sketch songwriting mode into 1990s Britpop.

signatureTracks.title: Country House
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Went head-to-head with Oasis's "Roll With It" in the same release week, a chart battle the UK press turned into the defining media event of Britpop.
